Subject: Interim notice — sustained p99 extension impacting streaming responses (US‑EAST)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Quick heads up: we’re observing a sustained extension in p99 response times for streaming generation on our US‑EAST serving pool that may impact real‑time features in your integration (notably the live summarization endpoint). We opened an incident (INC-20261121-US-EAST-STREAM) and our on‑call SREs are triaging.

Initial impact: ~3% of streaming requests are experiencing p99s that are 2–3x above normal (affected requests show stalled token flushes after ~600ms). This is primarily visible for sessions with >1k prefix tokens. No evidence of data loss; tokens eventually return.

What we’re doing now:
- SREs running targeted p95/p99 trace correlation to identify hotspot (Connor).
- Rolling a prioritized mitigation: temporary preference routing to warmed dedicated instances for affected customers (Marissa / ops).
- Collecting trace dumps and a snapshot (attached).

ETA for next update: 11:45 AM PT. We’ll provide a status page update and an ops advisory with short‑term mitigations.

We appreciate the urgency — I’ll make sure your team gets a clear remediation ETA as soon as Connor has correlation.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Interim notice — sustained p99 extension impacting streaming responses (US‑EAST)

Vanessa / Marissa —

Quick triage notes from SRE:
- Root signal: elevated tok_flush latency tied to KV cache eviction storms on a subset of nodes handling long‑prefix sessions. Evictions spike when parallel requests hit >4k warm cache entries; we see this primarily in us‑east-1a and 1b.
- Immediate mitigation we initiated at 09:28 PT: 1) adjust eviction threshold on affected pools; 2) route high‑prefix sessions to a warmed dedicated lane (best effort). Early telemetry shows a drop in new p99 events but tail remains for in‑flight sessions.
- Short workaround for customers: reduce prefix size to <800 tokens or retry streaming after 200–400ms backoff; we can do preferential routing for Luminate while we stabilize.

I’m attaching a quick trace dump and the runbook excerpt. If Marissa confirms Luminate wants preferential routing, we’ll add them to the warmed pool and monitor.

Connor O'Brien
SRE — Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai

Subject: Update / next steps — INC-20261121-US-EAST-STREAM

Hi Sam / Priya —

Short update following remediation:
- We saw measurable improvement after the warmed lane routing and eviction threshold bump. New session p99s in the warmed pool are back to baseline within 5–7 minutes.
- Affected in‑flight sessions are completing, but a small percentage (≈0.4%) saw truncated streams resulting in a partial event; we’ve flagged these for replay where possible.
- Root cause (preliminary): KV cache eviction storms caused by bursty long‑prefix traffic coinciding with an internal eviction algorithm regression introduced in last week’s kernel build (RED-4872).

Actions we’re taking:
1) Roll back the regression in canary (target: 14:00 PT) and progressively deploy the fix to us‑east.
2) Implement a temporary client advisory recommending prefix trimming and jittered retry patterns (we’ll send a short snippet you can paste in client code).
3) Postmortem and root‑cause writeup to be shared within 72 hours.

We’ve updated the public incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261121-US-EAST-STREAM — will add timeline + impact summary after full validation.

If you’d like us to provision a short burst-capacity window while we finish the rollback, I can get that approved immediately.

Thanks for the prompt reporting and patience — we’ll follow up with the postmortem and the client‑side helper snippet shortly.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
